42880152.label: Objectives
42880152.text: To evaluate whether post-chemoradiotherapy neoadjuvant chemotherapy Vesical Imaging-Reporting and Data System (nacVI-RADS) is associated with pathological complete response (pCR), and to assess its diagnostic performance and inter-reader agreement in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC).

42880152.label: Materials and methods
42880152.text: This retrospective study included 73 patients with non-metastatic cT2-4aN0-2 M0 bladder cancer who underwent cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy followed by radical or partial cystectomy between 2009 and 2024. Two radiologists independently assigned post-chemoradiotherapy nacVI-RADS scores on MRI. For the primary diagnostic analysis, scores were dichotomized as < 3 and ≥ 3. The reference standard was bladder pCR, defined as ypT0 on pathological assessment.

42880152.label: Results
42880152.text: pCR was achieved in 46 of 73 patients (63%). The pCR rate was higher among patients with nacVI-RADS < 3 than among those with nacVI-RADS ≥ 3 for both readers (reader 1: 77% vs. 39%, p = 0.002; reader 2: 74% vs. 39%, p = 0.008). The sensitivity and specificity of nacVI-RADS < 3 for identifying pCR were 78% and 59% for reader 1 and 80% and 52% for reader 2, respectively. Inter-reader agreement was excellent (κ = 0.845; 95% CI, 0.687-0.962).

42880152.label: Conclusion
42880152.text: Post-chemoradiotherapy nacVI-RADS < 3 was associated with pCR and showed moderate diagnostic performance with excellent inter-reader agreement in patients with MIBC. Post-chemoradiotherapy nacVI-RADS may provide useful complementary information for response assessment. Larger prospective multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings.

42891702.label: Purpose
42891702.text: To evaluate small field of view (FOV) ultra-high spatial resolution pelvic photon-counting detector prostate CT angiograms (UHR PCD CTA) for identifying prostate arterial anatomy and extraprostatic anastomoses in patients undergoing workup for prostate artery embolization (PAE).

42891702.label: Methods
42891702.text: IRB-approved retrospective imaging and electronic medical record review of men who consecutively underwent UHR PCD CTA for PAE workup at our institution from 8/1/2022 to 12/1/2024. UHR PCD CTAs were evaluated by two vascular and interventional radiologists for main and accessory candidate prostatic arteries (PA/s) and anastomoses to penile, bladder, or rectal arteries. A main PA was defined as supplying the central gland and an accessory PA was defined as supplying the peripheral zone. PAs were categorized using the Carnevale classification. In patients who proceeded to PAE, digital subtraction angiograms (DSA) were retrospectively compared with UHR PCD CTA findings.

42891702.label: Results
42891702.text: UHR PCD CTA was obtained prior to PAE consultation for 50 men. We evaluated 100 pelvic sides, identifying 180 candidate PAs with a median of 3 candidate PAs per patient (mean, 3.6; range, 2-7). Overall, 56% (101/180) of candidate PAs were main and 44% (79/180) were accessory. Abridged Carnevale classifications: Type 5-21% (38/180). Eight accessory candidate PAs arose from the superior rectal artery. At least one candidate anastomosis arose from 40% (72/180) of candidate PAs. Of 95 total candidate anastomoses, 69 were extraprostatic (30 rectal, 20 bladder, 19 penile) and 26 were intraprostatic collaterals; 56% (53/95) arose from accessory and 44% (42/95) from main candidate PAs. Twenty-eight of 50 (56%) men underwent PAE, during which 72% (74/103) of available candidate PAs were selected, and prostatic supply was confirmed by DSA in 100% (74/74) of selected vessels.

42891702.label: Conclusion
42891702.text: Small FOV UHR PCD CTA is useful in identifying candidate PA supply, as well as potential extraprostatic anastomoses, providing an arterial roadmap for PAE planning. Candidate PA supply was confirmed by DSA in all selected vessels among patients who proceeded to PAE.

42912552.text: The identification and diagnosis of aortic dissection on PET/CT remain challenging without the use of contrast agents. Such cases are prone to misdiagnosis or being overlooked, particularly when the examination is focused on an unrelated primary clinical objective. We present a case of thoracic aortic dissection that was incidentally detected on initial PET/CT during the further evaluation of suspected multiple myeloma. The FDG-avid lesion was initially mistaken for an esophageal mass, with differential diagnoses including extramedullary plasmacytoma associated with multiple myeloma and primary esophageal neoplasm.

42933252.label: Purpose
42933252.text: To develop and externally validate a CT-based clinicoradiological model for preoperative differentiation of pancreatic adenosquamous carcinoma (PASC) from pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC).

42933252.label: Materials and methods
42933252.text: This dual-center retrospective study included 397 patients with surgically confirmed PASC or PDAC and preoperative contrast-enhanced CT. In the development cohort, patients with PASC were matched 1:2 to patients with PDAC by age, sex, and tumor location. At the second center, consecutive eligible patients with PASC and PDAC identified during prespecified diagnosis-specific study periods constituted the external validation cohort. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression followed by multivariable logistic regression was used for model development.

42933252.label: Results
42933252.text: In the development cohort, the integrated model achieved an AUC of 0.919. In the external cohort, discrimination was preserved (AUC, 0.846; 95% CI, 0.781-0.910), but calibration was poor (slope, 0.445; 95% CI, 0.309-0.603). Calibration-in-the-large was 0.152 (95% CI, -0.358 to 0.656), with an observed-to-expected ratio of 1.03. The integrated model outperformed the clinical-only model (ΔAUC, 0.179; p < 0.001), whereas incremental discrimination beyond the imaging-only model was not demonstrated (ΔAUC, -0.004; p = 0.85). Decision curve analysis in the development cohort suggested potential net benefit across selected threshold probabilities.

42933252.label: Conclusion
42933252.text: The CT-based clinicoradiological model showed good external discrimination but substantial miscalibration, supporting its potential for preoperative risk stratification rather than individual probability estimation. Further recalibration and prospective validation in unselected, prevalence-representative populations are required before clinical use.

42949152.label: Purpose
42949152.text: Patients with recurrent high-grade glioma have poor prognosis and limited treatment options. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility and potential clinical benefit of 177 Lu-PSMA therapy in this patient population.

42949152.label: Patients and methods
42949152.text: Eligible patients were selected for treatment based on positive 68 Ga-PSMA-PET findings. 177 Lu-PSMA (7.4 GBq/200 mCi) was administered at 6-8-week intervals and continued as long as well-tolerated. The safety, tolerability, and efficacy of 177 Lu-PSMA were assessed in each treatment cycle using PET/MRI, SPECT/CT, blood tests, neurological tests, and patient-reported outcome measures.

42949152.label: Results
42949152.text: Ten patients were enrolled (WHO grade 4 glioblastoma, n=6; WHO grade 4 astrocytoma, n=1; WHO grade 3 astrocytoma, n=3). 68 Ga-PSMA-PET before treatment demonstrated tumor uptake in 9 patients (median SUV max : 6.4, IQR: 4.2-9.0). Six patients received treatment (20 cycles total; range: 1-7 per patient). Median absorbed dose per cycle was 0.9 Gy (IQR: 0.8-1.1) for tumors, 2.6 Gy (IQR: 1.9-3.2) for kidneys, and 1.7 Gy (IQR: 1.5-2.2) for parotid glands. No CTCAE grade 3-4 toxicities occurred. The most common patient-reported symptoms were fatigue, transient xerostomia, and nausea. Median survival from treatment initiation was 187 days (range: 87-756) and the median progression-free survival was 45 days (range: 41-335). MRI (RANO 2.0) demonstrated stable disease in half of the patients during all or part of the treatment course.

42949152.label: Conclusions
42949152.text: 177 Lu-PSMA therapy was feasible and well-tolerated. Radiologic stabilization was observed in a subset of patients, but strategies to increase tumor dose delivery may be needed to improve efficacy.

43018702.text: Acute pancreatitis (AP) has a highly variable clinical course. This narrative review focuses on computed tomography (CT) radiomics, deep learning and clinical-imaging models for severity and adverse-outcome prediction, with clinical-only models as context. A targeted PubMed search checked on 16 October 2026, with a publication cutoff of 14 October 2026, retrieved 80 unique records; ten CT-informed exemplars and eight clinical-context studies were selected for detailed comparison. This is a representative, non-exhaustive synthesis. For severe AP (SAP) prediction, reported same-center internal or temporal areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) ranged from 0.852 to 0.894, and reported external-test AUCs from 0.887 to 0.916; one validation cohort of unconfirmed independence had an AUC of 0.920. These descriptive ranges do not establish model superiority or characterize all retrieved studies. CT protocols and input timing, endpoint definitions, sampling and validation designs varied. Predominantly retrospective evidence, uncertain prediction landmarks, incomplete calibration and threshold reporting, and limited prospective impact assessment constrain translation. Feature explanations describe model associations rather than causal intervention targets. Imaging artificial intelligence (AI) remains an adjunct to clinical assessment; independent validation, calibration, decision-curve appraisal and prospective workflow/outcome evaluation are needed before clinical-pathway integration.

43021502.label: Aims
43021502.text: Heart failure (HF) prevention remains limited because early multisystem cardiometabolic dysfunction is not captured by conventional risk tools. We evaluated whether liver radiomic phenotypes derived opportunistically from coronary artery calcium computed tomography (CAC-CT) identify imaging-defined hepatic stress states associated with incident HF.

43021502.label: Methods and results
43021502.text: We analysed 59 237 individuals undergoing CAC-CT (CLARIFY: 46 028; Houston Methodist: 13 209). Liver regions were segmented and radiomic features extracted to derive a Liver Radiomics Score (LRS). The model was trained in a CLARIFY derivation cohort (Dtr, n = 9205), validated in a hold-out cohort (Dts, n = 36 823), and externally evaluated in Houston Methodist (Dext, n = 13 209). The mean follow-up was 1411 days (SD 760.1) in the pooled Dtr and Dts cohorts (1144 HF events) and 470 days (SD 596) in Dext (212 HF events). Continuous LRS was associated with incident HF [Dts: hazard ratio (HR) 1.63, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.52-1.74; P < 0.001; Dext: HR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.07; P = 0.004] and remained significant after multivariable adjustment in Dts. Increasing LRS quartiles showed progressively adverse hepatic, haemodynamic, and cardiometabolic profiles and higher HF risk. Among 17 806 Dts participants with PREVENT data, adding LRS modestly improved discrimination across CAC- and PREVENT-based models (P < 0.001) and improved reclassification metrics (7-year net reclassification improvement up to 0.25; including integrated discrimination improvement up to 0.015). High LRS identified elevated risk in low-risk groups: among participants with CAC=0, high LRS conferred ∼2.5-fold higher 5-year HF incidence, and ∼2.9-fold in PREVENT-low individuals.

43021502.label: Conclusion
43021502.text: In this large multicentre cohort, liver radiomics from CAC-CT captured hepatic stress states linked to HF risk and modestly improved risk stratification beyond CAC and PREVENT scores.

43050052.label: Background
43050052.text: Pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas (PPGLs) frequently overexpress somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SSTR2), making [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT a promising functional imaging modality. However, the optimal interpretation criteria for distinguishing PPGL from non-PPGL lesions in clinically suspected adrenal or retroperitoneal masses remain undefined. This retrospective study evaluated the diagnostic performance of [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT by systematically comparing three interpretation criteria: Integrated Interpretation (combining PET/CT metabolic patterns, CT morphology, and clinical information), Liver Threshold Interpretation (lesion SUVmax ≥ liver SUVmean), and Blood-Pool Threshold Interpretation (lesion SUVmax ≥ 5 × blood-pool SUVmean). Thirty-six patients with suspected adrenal or retroperitoneal PPGL underwent [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT; all target lesions were histopathologically confirmed. Sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and ROC analyses were performed.

43050052.label: Results
43050052.text: Histopathology confirmed PPGL in 22 patients (18 adrenal, 4 extra-adrenal) and non-PPGL in 14 patients. The Liver Threshold Interpretation achieved 100% sensitivity (22/22), 78.6% specificity (11/14), and 91.7% accuracy (33/36), significantly outperforming the Integrated Interpretation in sensitivity (100% vs. 77.3%, P = 0.018), negative predictive value (100% vs. 70.6%, P = 0.047), and accuracy (91.7% vs. 80.6%, P < 0.001). The AUC of Liver Threshold (0.893) was significantly larger than those of Integrated (0.815, P = 0.042) and Blood-Pool (0.714, P = 0.014). Optimal cutoffs were SUVmax ≥ 6.95 (AUC 0.893) and lesion-to-liver ratio ≥ 0.95 (AUC 0.893). PPGL lesions showed higher SUVmax (24.4 ± 19.1 vs. 5.3 ± 3.5, P = 0.001) and smaller volumes. The 'target sign' (ring-like peripheral uptake) was more frequent in PPGLs (45.5% vs. 7.1%, P = 0.025).

43050052.label: Conclusion
43050052.text: [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy in distinguishing PPGL from non-PPGL lesions in clinically suspected adrenal or retroperitoneal masses. The Liver Threshold Interpretation is a practical screening tool with 100% sensitivity and 91.7% accuracy. Optimal semiquantitative cutoffs (lesion SUVmax ≥ 6.95 or lesion-to-liver ratio ≥ 0.95) provide reliable discrimination.

43079102.label: Background and aims
43079102.text: [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab is a PET radiotracer targeting carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX), a biomarker highly expressed in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). Following the high diagnostic accuracy demonstrated in the phase III ZIRCON trial, this study evaluated the real-world clinical performance and management impact of [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT in patients with indeterminate renal masses and advanced ccRCC.

43079102.label: Patients and methods
43079102.text: Within an early access program, patients with renal lesions of uncertain origin underwent [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT for noninvasive lesion characterization, while patients with advanced ccRCC were imaged for postoperative assessment, recurrence evaluation, or metastatic restaging. Following intravenous administration of 37 MBq (± 10%) [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab, PET/CT was performed on day 5 post-injection. Findings were correlated with histopathology where available, and their impact on clinical management was assessed retrospectively.

43079102.label: Results
43079102.text: Twenty-eight patients (22 men, 6 women; mean age, 71 ± 9 years) were included: 18 with indeterminate renal masses (Group A) and 10 undergoing postoperative, metastatic, or restaging evaluation (Group B). In Group A, PET/CT demonstrated CAIX-positive findings in 10/18 patients (56%) and CAIX-negative findings in 7/18 (39%); one patient showed heterogeneous tracer uptake. Histopathological confirmation was available in 11/18 patients (61%). Within this verified subset, patient-level PET/CT findings were concordant with histopathology, with all CAIX-positive patients (6/6) confirmed as ccRCC and all CAIX-negative patients (5/5) confirmed as non-ccRCC or benign. At the lesion level, however, concordance was incomplete in one patient: four CAIX-avid lesions were identified, two of which were confirmed as ccRCC, while the remaining two corresponded to an angiomyolipoma and normal renal parenchyma. PET/CT findings were associated with a subsequent change in the documented management plan in 11/18 patients (61%; 95% CI, 35.7-82.7%). In the exploratory Group B cohort, [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT demonstrated the presence or absence of detectable CAIX-avid findings and contributed to therapeutic and surveillance decisions.

43079102.label: Conclusions
43079102.text: In this real-world cohort, [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT showed concordance with histopathology in the limited verified subset and was associated with changes in clinical management, supporting further prospective evaluation in indeterminate renal masses and advanced ccRCC.

43102602.label: Purpose
43102602.text: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP)-related metabolic patterns on 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) can aid diagnosis of PSP. Given that many PSP variants evolve toward the prototypic PSP-Richardson's syndrome (PSP-RS) phenotype during disease progression, a PSP-RS-related pattern (richardsonPSPRP) may capture an essential disease signature. We evaluated whether expression of a richardsonPSPRP reflects disease severity and longitudinal clinical progression in prospective Korean PSP cohorts.

43102602.label: Methods
43102602.text: We derived Korean richardsonPSPRP from probable PSP-RS (n = 20) and HC (n = 24) with external validation in a Taiwanese PSP-RS cohort (n = 32). We estimated individual richardsonPSPRP expression z-scores in 81 patients with PSP (55 PSP-RS and 26 variants) and 77 with PD. The diagnostic and prognostic capabilities of richardsonPSPRP z-score were investigated with clinical measures both cross-sectionally and longitudinally using correlation analyses and linear mixed-effects models.

43102602.label: Results
43102602.text: The richardsonPSPRP excellently discriminated PSP-RS from HC in the derivation and Taiwanese validation cohorts (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] = 0.99 for both) and differentiated PSP from PD (AUROC = 0.90). Higher richardsonPSPRP expression correlated with greater disease severity (PSP rating scale: r = 0.61; PSP clinical deficits scale: r = 0.47), poorer cognition (Mini-Mental State Examination: r=-0.56; Montreal Cognitive Assessment: r=-0.54) and activities of daily living (r=-0.62). Higher baseline richardsonPSPRP z-score predicted faster longitudinal progression on the PSP rating scale (β = 0.25, P = 0.0028) and PSP clinical deficits scale (β = 0.062, P = 0.0038) in overall and variant PSP cohorts.

43102602.label: Conclusions
43102602.text: The richardsonPSPRP expression may be useful for assessing disease burden across the PSP spectrum, warranting validation in large multicenter cohorts.
